}
NEnvP_52:
"Goal/Purpose": "To recognize local, traditional and indigenous knowledge and practices for their contribution to the conservation of ecosystem services and for upholding cultural, religious and social values; and to harness them for better environmental and social outcomes.",
"Action/Intervention": "Recognize local, traditional and indigenous knowledge and practices relating to environmental management; take necessary measures to adopt local, traditional and indigenous knowledge/practices as a whole or in combination with modern science-based practices for sustainable management of land, water, air and biodiversity resources, adaptation to climate change impacts, and disaster mitigation; initiate action to compile, document, conserve and create public awareness on local, traditional and indigenous knowledge and practices; revisit activities that result in the gradual loss of such knowledge with suitable national mechanism in line with international Conventions and Protocols.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Environmental management; conservation of ecosystem services; sustainable management of land, water, air and biodiversity resources; climate change adaptation; disaster mitigation.",
"Target Audience": "Local, traditional and indigenous knowledge holders and practitioners; those involved in environmental management; national mechanisms.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Recognition of the contribution of local, traditional and indigenous knowledge and practices to conservation of ecosystem services and cultural, religious and social values; adoption of such knowledge and practices alone or with modern science-based practices; improved public awareness; conservation and documentation of knowledge and practices; reduced gradual loss of local, traditional and indigenous knowledge; better environmental and social outcomes."
NEnvP_53:
"Goal/Purpose": "To mainstream consultation of local stakeholders and community organizations in environmental management, enhance participation of NGOs, CSOs, CBOs, women and youth groups including differently-abled and those with special needs, mobilize community organizations in conserving soil, water, air and biodiversity resources, and give special attention to female and youth participation and empowerment in environmental management.",
"Action/Intervention": "Mainstream consultation of local stakeholders (rural and urban) and community organizations in the preparation and implementation of management plans; enhance participation of NGOs, CSOs, CBOs, women and youth groups including differently-abled and those with special needs in implementing policy measures and environmental management plans by building partnerships and delegating decision-making powers; mobilize community organizations through awareness creation, training, education, and provision of supportive facilities; give special attention to female and youth participation and empowerment in community and stakeholder engagement activities.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Environmental management, including management plans and the conservation of soil, water, air and biodiversity resources.",
"Target Audience": "Local stakeholders (rural and urban), community organizations, NGOs, CSOs, CBOs, women and youth groups, differently-abled people, those with special needs, females, and youth.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Successful implementation of policy measures and environmental management plans, better environmental and social outcomes, active community role in conserving soil, water, air and biodiversity resources, and enhanced female and youth participation and empowerment in environmental management."
NEnvP_54:
"Goal/Purpose": "To develop the capacity of provincial and local government officers to handle environment-related issues, raise public awareness on environmental issues and the values of the environment including biodiversity and ecosystem services, and periodically update environmental content in the national education curriculum at all levels.",
"Action/Intervention": "Provide well-designed training programmes through a coordinated and planned approach for provincial and local government officers, especially on data management and identification of key actions to be implemented; undertake campaigns on targeted environmental issues in printed and electronic public media and social media channels, including awareness on biodiversity, ecosystem services, Environmental Impact Assessments, and Environmental Protection Licenses; update environmental content in the national education curriculum at all levels by introducing selected topics and enriching existing topics with new facts with the support of education professionals.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Environment, including biodiversity and ecosystem services; national education curriculum; environmental permitting.",
"Target Audience": "Provincial and local government officers, the public, and learners at all levels of the national education system (early childhood, school, technical/vocational, and higher education), with support from education professionals.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Improved capacity of provincial and local government officers to address environment-related issues; increased public awareness of environmental issues, environmental values, biodiversity, ecosystem services, and permit-related processes; and periodically updated environmental content in the national education curriculum at all levels."
NEnvP_55:
"Goal/Purpose": "To streamline Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) procedures, strengthen their scope and administration, and improve public consultation, transparency, and monitoring in evaluating investment plans and projects.",
"Action/Intervention": "Streamline EIA and SEA procedures for evaluating investment plans and projects; improve public consultation; increase transparency; establish continuous pre- and post-monitoring to minimize unethical conduct; strengthen EIAs and SEAs to include socio-economic, political, and cultural dimensions in addition to physical and biological dimensions; strengthen the capacity and technical capability of the Central Environment Authority (CEA) and other relevant agencies to administer EIAs and SEAs and monitor industrial activities for compliance with existing EIA laws and regulations.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) processes for investment plans, projects, and industrial activities.",
"Target Audience": "Central Environment Authority (CEA) and other relevant agencies; stakeholders involved in investment plans and projects; industrial activities subject to EIA laws and regulations; the public involved in consultation processes.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Improved public consultation, increased transparency, continuous pre- and post-monitoring, minimized unethical conduct, broader inclusion of socio-economic, political, cultural, physical, and biological dimensions in EIAs and SEAs, and strengthened agency capacity and technical capability to administer assessments and monitor compliance with existing laws and regulations."
NEneP_1:
"Goal/Purpose": "To secure the primary and secondary energy resources and supplies used in the country in order to maximise energy supply reliability, continuity, adequacy, and strategic independence.",
"Action/Intervention": "Ensure diversity in energy resources used in electricity generation subject to economic, environmental, technological and operational requirements; use natural gas as the next fossil fuel option to broaden diversity considering recent price profiles; establish a liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal of optimum size and technology at the most suitable location, with operation of the first terminal and LNG procurement kept under state control; pursue global diversification of energy sources to safeguard the supply chain against external geopolitical uncertainties; limit installed power generation capacity from a single imported fuel to not more than 50% of total installed firm capacity; ensure adequacy and reliability of transmission and distribution infrastructure in electricity and fuel supply networks to meet future contingencies; conduct regular risk assessments to identify and mitigate internal and external contingencies affecting energy sector performance; explore indigenous petroleum resources using geophysical surveys and strengthen the national petroleum data repository; strategically develop indigenous petroleum resources for use in power generation, transport, household and industry, and for cleaner energy sources such as hydrogen and gas to liquids (GTL); meet national electricity requirements with proven generation technologies and fuel sources; make maintenance of strategic fuel reserves in strategic locations mandatory for key players in the electricity and petroleum industries; expand local crude oil refining capacity to optimally satisfy demand for petroleum products; pursue viable cross-border electricity transmission and regional cooperation based on multilateral power pool operation.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Energy sector, including electricity generation, fuel supply networks, petroleum, transmission and distribution infrastructure, and cross-border electricity cooperation.",
"Target Audience": "Key players in the electricity and petroleum industries, the state, and entities involved in energy supply, infrastructure, petroleum resource development, refining, and regional electricity cooperation.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Secured energy resources and supplies; improved reliability, continuity and adequacy of national energy supply; greater strategic independence; reduced exposure to geopolitical uncertainties and fuel price shocks; strengthened transmission and distribution resilience; expanded indigenous petroleum resource development and refining capacity; mandatory strategic fuel reserves; and enhanced regional electricity cooperation."
NEneP_2:
"Goal/Purpose": "Provide all citizens with access to reliable, convenient, affordable, equitable and quality energy services in order to enhance living standards and enable engagement in gainful economic activities.",
"Action/Intervention": "Ensure access to electricity through on-grid or off-grid sources and to modern petroleum products for all citizens; support small and medium enterprises by socialising part of initial electricity service connection costs via tariffs; connect households that remain unconnected to the national grid due to unaffordability through innovative financing schemes; encourage new productive uses for electricity in agriculture, rural and primary industries with emphasis on empowerment of women and youth; improve supply quality of energy services by electricity, gas and oil utilities through adoption of appropriate technical and commercial quality standards; introduce minimum service quality standards for common utility services and offer premium services for customers willing to pay for higher service quality levels; standardise equipment used in the energy supply chain to ensure compatibility, ease of integration and safety; gradually place electricity distribution networks underground in urban areas and convert them to insulated aerial bundled conductors in other areas; promote pipeline transport and vehicle-based transport in the downstream gas and oil supply sector to improve access by industries and households and feed appropriate distribution networks at the user end; introduce smart grid technologies and deploy smart metering to enhance customer experience and automate power system management where manual intervention is uneconomical; introduce mobile and internet-based services to enhance customer convenience.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Energy services sector, including electricity, gas and oil supply, distribution and utility services.",
"Target Audience": "All citizens; households; small and medium enterprises; industries; agriculture, rural and primary industries; women and youth; customers of electricity, gas and oil utilities.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Universal access to electricity and modern petroleum products; improved affordability of connections for households and small and medium enterprises; improved quality, reliability, safety, compatibility and convenience of energy services; enhanced customer experience and automated power system management; improved access to gas and oil distribution networks for industries and households; increased productive use of electricity in agriculture, rural and primary industries; enhanced living standards and greater participation in gainful economic activities."
NEneP_3:
"Goal/Purpose": "To provide energy services at the optimum long-term cost in order to lower the burden on the national economy and achieve competitiveness of locally produced goods and services in international markets.",
"Action/Intervention": "Implement power plants identified in the Long-Term Generation Expansion Plan as scheduled; identify and develop in time the receiving, processing, storage, transport and distribution capacity requirements of the petroleum sector through long-term planning to ensure adequate supply of petroleum products; adopt rational energy pricing strategies based on cost reflectivity across the energy value chain through existing and new regulatory mechanisms; identify and provide transparently funded subsidies to target groups of energy users in household, industrial and commercial sectors that deserve special consideration owing to their economic standing and contribution to national economic development priorities.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Energy sector, including electricity generation and the petroleum sector.",
"Target Audience": "Sector utilities; household, industrial and commercial energy users; producers of locally produced goods and services; the national economy.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Energy services provided at optimum long-term cost; reduced burden on the national economy; improved competitiveness of locally produced goods and services in international markets; adequate supply of petroleum products; financial health of sector utilities; discouraged wasteful energy use; transparently funded subsidies provided to specified target groups of energy users."
NEneP_4:
"Goal/Purpose": "To ensure energy systems are effectively managed for the efficient use and conservation of energy, and to pursue efficient energy use by all concerned, from utilities to final customers.",
"Action/Intervention": "Strengthen the national energy efficiency improvement and conservation programme engaging stakeholders in household, industrial and commercial sectors; promote energy efficiency and conservation through minimum energy performance standards and appliance labelling, and introduce green procurement processes in state and private sector organisations; launch a home productivity improvement programme with energy efficiency and conservation as the central theme to empower women; introduce taxation and other incentives and disincentives to support the market for efficient technologies; offer expert energy advisory services through state and private sector service providers to promote energy efficiency, conservation and energy cost reduction across end-use sectors; recognize water resources as a valuable indigenous energy resource and enhance efficient use of water by competing users where water has a high opportunity cost; enhance conversion efficiency of power generation facilities; formulate a strategic plan for street lighting to improve management, road user safety, aesthetics and energy conservation; consider automated demand response technologies as a main demand-side management strategy; reduce losses in energy delivery networks to optimum levels; reduce losses in petroleum refining through continuous technology infusion with new investments; reduce transport fuel use in petroleum distribution by using regional storage facilities connected with the rail-based supply network; promote virtual offices and video/teleconferencing through changes to organisational working culture to minimize physical movement; reduce transport energy use through avoid, shift and improve strategies with a strong focus on high quality public transport and intelligent traffic management solutions; develop economic activities in dense clusters in special zones identified as smart cities, served by smart grids, to lower logistic costs and improve synergies; use sustainable neighbourhoods as a key design element in urban development to reduce energy demand; make energy efficiency a primary concern in retrofits and evaluate new building designs for energy performance on a mandatory basis; ensure smart technologies, including smart buildings and complete conversion to smart metering, to convey price signals to customers and alter demand profiles to reduce overall supply cost; and consider vehicle fuel efficiency in applicable vehicle taxes to encourage a higher-efficiency vehicle fleet.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Energy systems, including household, industrial and commercial sectors, power generation, energy delivery networks, petroleum refining and distribution, transport, urban development, buildings, water resource use, street lighting, and smart city/grid systems.",
"Target Audience": "Utilities, final customers, stakeholders in household, industrial and commercial sectors, state and private sector organisations, women, state and private sector service providers, competing water users, road users, customers, and vehicle owners/users.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Effective management of energy systems; improved energy efficiency and conservation; reduced energy costs; enhanced efficient use of water where opportunity cost is high; improved conversion efficiency of power generation facilities; reduced losses in energy delivery networks and petroleum refining; reduced transport fuel and transport energy use; improved management of street lighting with contributions to road safety and aesthetics; reduced energy demand in urban development and buildings; altered demand profiles and reduced overall cost of supply through smart technologies and metering; and a higher-efficiency vehicle fleet."
NEneP_5:
"Goal/Purpose": "To develop indigenous energy resources to optimum levels to minimise dependence on imported resources, minimise the vulnerability of energy supplies to external situations, and attain a higher degree of resilience in the energy sector, subject to resolving technical, economic, environmental and social constraints.",
"Action/Intervention": "Explore the country’s oil and natural gas resources and strategically phase commercial-scale exploitation with consideration of higher future value and possible future use as a locally available fuel source for cleaner energy sources such as hydrogen; explore, assess and keep ready for development indigenous mineral resources such as Thorianite and other similar nuclear fuels with commercial resource potential when conversion technologies are available; exploit renewable energy resources based on a priority order considering economics, technology and resource quality; enhance biomass availability through dedicated energy plantations or plantations with residue in prescribed biomass energy development areas; encourage commercial availability of biomass and biomass-based fuel products for industrial thermal applications and household use; facilitate processed biomass through efficient collection, processing, value addition, storage, distribution and biomass supply chains; introduce and promote improved biomass conversion devices such as cook stoves for household use; encourage gradual diversification of rail and road transport energy from oil to electricity; offer appropriate time-of-use tariffs to attract electric vehicle charging during lower-demand periods and use added demand to enhance integration of indigenous sources such as solar and wind; channel a sizable fund to the Sri Lanka Sustainable Energy Fund through a cess on fossil fuel imports and a resource royalty from renewable resources and broaden the purposes of the fund to meet sustainable energy, electricity and petroleum sector requirements; recognise the contribution of the rubber plantation industry as a major fuel wood supplier for thermal applications and provide incentives to enhance the expanse of rubber plantations.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Energy sector, including indigenous energy resources, renewable energy, biomass energy, transport energy, electricity, petroleum, and industrial and household fuel use.",
"Target Audience": "Energy sector institutions, the Sri Lanka Sustainable Energy Authority and Sri Lanka Sustainable Energy Fund, fossil fuel importers, renewable resource users, transport sector actors in rail and road transport, industrial and household energy users, biomass supply chain actors, and the rubber plantation industry.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Reduced dependence on imported energy resources; reduced vulnerability of energy supplies to external situations; higher resilience in the energy sector; increased exploration and readiness of indigenous oil, gas and nuclear fuel resources; increased exploitation of renewable energy resources; enhanced biomass availability and supply chains; greater use of improved biomass cook stoves; increased electrification of transport; improved integration of indigenous solar and wind sources through electric vehicle charging demand management; increased funding for sustainable energy; and enhanced fuel wood supply from rubber plantations."
NEneP_6:
"Goal/Purpose": "Preserve the natural environment of the country and make a meaningful contribution to addressing climate change by adopting appropriate low emission processes and mitigation measures.",
"Action/Intervention": "Minimise and mitigate environmental impacts of energy facilities using counter balancing interventions such as carbon sequestration plantations, including in existing hydropower catchments and land earmarked for future energy infrastructure; minimise climate change-related environmental impacts from the construction and operation of energy sector facilities; encourage energy supply from cleaner sources and technologies while considering impacts on the national economy and long-term environmental benefits; develop indigenous petroleum and nuclear energy resources to the optimum level with sufficient environmental safeguards by encouraging market demand; implement national level plans to utilise commercially valuable by-products from power generation such as fly ash and waste heat; make Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) to meet agreed national emission reduction obligations; study and factor local social and environmental externalities of the energy sector into decision making; exploit opportunities under carbon trading mechanisms and implement a proper mechanism to use this potential; favourably consider waste-to-energy projects for municipal solid waste disposal, with any cost above the avoided cost of electricity paid by government/local authorities directly to the developer; introduce necessary Health, Safety and Environmental (HSE) standards and enforce relevant regulations, including making it an offence to operate energy-related infrastructure without complying with prescribed HSE standards.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Natural environment of the country; climate change mitigation; energy sector; hydropower catchments; land earmarked for future energy infrastructure; municipal solid waste management.",
"Target Audience": "Energy sector decision makers and operators; government and local authorities; developers of energy-related infrastructure and waste-to-energy projects.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Environmental impacts of energy sector facilities are minimised and mitigated; cleaner energy sources and technologies are encouraged; commercially valuable power generation by-products are utilised; national emission reduction obligations under NDCs are met; carbon trading opportunities are used; municipal solid waste is disposed through waste-to-energy projects; and compliance with HSE standards in energy-related infrastructure is enforced."
NEneP_7:
"Goal/Purpose": "Increase the share of energy supply from renewable energy resources in the country’s energy mix to reduce pressure on foreign exchange, engage the local community in the energy industry, attain sustainability, and promote the use of environmentally friendly energy sources.",
"Action/Intervention": "Reduce delays in renewable energy development through a centrally coordinated project approval process; realise renewable energy investments for electricity generation through a competitive scheme to reduce costs and facilitate wider investor participation; strengthen transmission infrastructure to improve absorption of electricity generation from renewable sources; upgrade distribution infrastructure with smart grid technologies to facilitate renewable energy-based distributed generation; conduct research to overcome adverse impacts of renewable energy absorption to the power system from intermittent sources such as wind and solar energy; introduce effective forecasting technologies for wind, solar and rainfall to optimise use of renewable resources; encourage energy storage solutions for firming intermittent renewable sources, voltage and frequency regulation, local grid support, peak shaving and improving grid resilience; introduce innovative financing schemes and financial instruments involving both public and private enterprises to encourage renewable energy development.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Energy sector, specifically renewable energy supply, electricity generation, transmission and distribution infrastructure, and power system management.",
"Target Audience": "Public and private enterprises involved in renewable energy development and investment, electricity sector institutions responsible for project approval, transmission and distribution infrastructure, local communities, and investors.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "An increased share of renewable energy in the national energy mix, reduced delays in renewable energy development, lower electricity generation costs, wider investor participation, improved grid absorption and integration of renewable electricity, enhanced distributed generation, better management of intermittency through research, forecasting and storage, improved grid resilience, reduced pressure on foreign exchange, greater local community engagement in the energy industry, and increased use of environmentally friendly energy sources."
NEneP_8:
"Goal/Purpose": "To make good governance the guiding principle in all aspects of the energy sector and strengthen it to realise accountability, fairness and transparency, thereby achieving investor and consumer confidence. To establish and further strengthen a stable policy environment and regulatory frameworks to assure good governance in the energy sector.",
"Action/Intervention": "Bring all sub sectors in the energy industry under respective regulatory framework; procure plant, equipment, crude oil, other fuels, power purchase agreements and similar concessions through a streamlined competitive bidding scheme ensuring transparency, accountability and avoiding long term delays; enhance capability of energy sector professionals through exchange programmes with similar foreign entities and cross posting within Sri Lankan sector entities; prioritise digitalisation of energy sector entities using an enterprise resource planning platform across the value chain from smart meters, addressable appliances and smart grids, allowing adoption of AI, IoT and distributed ledgers to drive efficiency, transparency and optimisation of asset utilisation; introduce a guideline on management of digital information covering secure storing, use and management; use digitalisation of utility transactions to secure and store data in cloud based central databases and index, catalogue and securely store sector data, information and knowledge as knowledge assets; create a conducive environment for independent decision making in a transparent and accountable manner supported by analyses using real time insights produced by digitalisation; require relevant entities to report energy sector transactions to the SEA on a fixed annual schedule through a working group of officials from key sector institutions to ensure timely publication of the Sri Lanka Energy Balance; identify indices that assist understanding of energy sector trends and include them in national statistics to support evidence-based decision making; promote active engagement of citizens in the energy sector using web portals linked to mobile phone applications for awareness creation, grievance handling and education, targeting closure of trust deficit, greater acceptance of energy sector projects, user safety and improved end-user behaviour of energy services.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Energy sector",
"Target Audience": "Energy sector entities and professionals; relevant entities reporting to the SEA; officials from key sector institutions; citizens, investors and consumers",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Strengthened accountability, fairness and transparency in the energy sector; investor and consumer confidence; a stable policy environment and stronger regulatory frameworks; transparent and accountable procurement with reduced long term delays; enhanced professional capability; improved efficiency, transparency and optimisation of asset utilisation through digitalisation; secure management, storage and use of digital information and knowledge assets; more independent, transparent and accountable decision making supported by real time analysis; timely publication of the Sri Lanka Energy Balance; improved evidence-based decision making through sector indices in national statistics; increased citizen awareness and engagement, better grievance handling, reduced trust deficit, greater acceptance of energy sector projects, improved user safety and improved end-user behaviour of energy services."
NEneP_9:
"Goal/Purpose": "To earmark and secure in advance strategic locations required for future energy infrastructure, considering land limitations and past financial losses from shifting sites, in order to ensure timely implementation of facilities and minimise adverse social impacts.",
"Action/Intervention": "Strategically earmark suitable sites in advance for future energy infrastructure such as coal, natural gas and nuclear power plants, refineries and terminals following preliminary feasibility studies; identify and mark on a master plan the best sites for large-scale renewable energy infrastructure such as wind and solar farms for phased development as concentrated facilities; identify corridors for petroleum and gas pipe transport and backbone electricity transmission, giving priority to shared corridors; publish identified routes to provide advance information to the public; use available corridors to lay multiple pipelines and power transmission lines wherever possible; make all existing and future underground utility infrastructure, including electricity, water, communication, town gas and petroleum, available in a common mandatory geographic information system (GIS); and coordinate roadside utility infrastructure corridors with transport infrastructure to ensure clear demarcation of ownership, flexibility of maintenance, and room for expansion.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Energy infrastructure planning, utility corridor planning, underground utility infrastructure, and transport-coordinated infrastructure development.",
"Target Audience": "National infrastructure planners, relevant public authorities responsible for energy, utilities and transport infrastructure, and the public.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Timely implementation of future energy infrastructure; reduced financial losses associated with shifting sites; minimal relocation and social impacts during actual development; advance public awareness of identified routes and sites; optimal location of future underground cable routes and pipe transport traces; and improved coordination, maintenance flexibility, ownership clarity, and expansion capacity for utility infrastructure corridors."
NEneP_10:
"Goal/Purpose": "To utilise the relative vastness of the energy sector in Sri Lanka to nurture local entrepreneurship and innovation, particularly to support technology-intensive local businesses despite limitations in the scale of available markets.",
"Action/Intervention": "Recognise electricity as the dominant energy carrier of the future; nurture strategic ventures that use local resources in energy conversion and storage equipment as an industrialisation thrust; encourage development of novel ICT applications for power system automation, remote control, distributed real-time event and data acquisition systems, and smart metering; encourage Sri Lankan enterprises to engage in energy sector infrastructure development; promote research and development on introducing, adopting and implementing new and emerging renewable fuel sources, efficient energy conversion and end-use technologies; facilitate innovation through intellectual property protection, safeguarding innovations until commercialisation, and providing financial incentives and tax benefits for nascent technologies; realise indigenous knowledge and capacities required for energy sector development; study the potential of vehicle energy storage systems as local standby energy storage, automated demand response options, and load profile management tools; encourage small-scale on-grid distributed and off-grid stand-alone renewable energy applications with local value addition as an economic development thrust.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Energy sector in Sri Lanka, including electricity, renewable energy, energy conversion and storage, ICT applications for power systems, and energy infrastructure development.",
"Target Audience": "Local entrepreneurs, innovators, Sri Lankan enterprises, researchers and developers, and actors involved in energy sector development.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Nurturing of local entrepreneurship and innovation in the energy sector; increased engagement of Sri Lankan enterprises in energy infrastructure development; promotion of new ICT and renewable energy technologies; support for commercialisation of nascent technologies through intellectual property protection and incentives; and encouragement of distributed and stand-alone renewable energy applications with local value addition."
